Affiliation:: University of Oklahoma, Stephenson School of Biomedical Engineering; University of Oklahoma, School of Electrical and Computer Engineering
Techniques Used: Phase Retrieval Algorithm with Pupil Function Recovery
Data & Platforms: Peripheral Blood Samples from Leukemia Patients
Application Areas: Breast Cancer Screening and Risk Stratification
Key Research Thinking Patterns: Computational Super-Resolution via Aperture Synthesis: Replacing high-NA physical optics with computational reconstruction to achieve oil-immersion-free, high-resolution wide-field imaging of biological samples (e.g., Fourier Ptychography Microscopy with NAeq 1.11 for metaphase chromosome imaging).

Asymmetry-Driven Bilateral Feature Fusion: Leveraging the physiological symmetry of paired organs to detect pathology by analyzing feature differences between unregistered multi-view mammograms (e.g., bilateral asymmetry analysis and ipsilateral view correspondence modeling).

Robust Semi-Supervised Deep Learning: Enhancing model generalizability and diagnostic accuracy in data-scarce clinical settings by integrating unlabeled data through perturbation-based regularization (e.g., Virtual Adversarial Training and Local Distribution Smoothness for breast mass classification).

Multi-View Transformer Architecture Design: Utilizing self-attention mechanisms across multiple imaging perspectives to capture complex spatial relationships and improve classification performance (e.g., Multi-view Vision Transformers with local/global blocks for mammogram analysis).
Summary Description: Liu Hong bridges biomedical engineering and computational imaging to advance diagnostic automation in oncology and hematology. In breast cancer screening, the researcher employs multi-view vision transformers and bilateral asymmetry analysis to detect occult tumors and stratify risk in dense tissue, utilizing semi-supervised learning to maximize utility from unlabeled clinical data. In cytogenetics, Liu develops high-numerical-aperture Fourier ptychography microscopy, enabling oil-immersion-free, high-throughput imaging of metaphase chromosomes for automated leukemia diagnosis. By integrating advanced computational microscopy with deep learning frameworks, this work significantly enhances resolution, throughput, and diagnostic efficiency in both breast cancer and hematological malignancies.
